newsitem.title: CHINA: China corn sale to Philippines said done at $157/T.
newsitem.headline: China corn sale to Philippines said done at $157/T.

text.p: China has concluded the sale of 145,000 tonnes of corn to the Philippines on a governmment-to-government basis at US$157 a tonne C&F, a U.S. government source told Reuters on Wednesday.

The source said the sale, for February to April shipment, was priced at a significantly higher level than current U.S. corn export quotes to the region and was also above other recent Chinese corn sales.

U.S. trader Cargill on Tuesday sold 52,500 tonnes of corn to South Korea's NLCF at $135.60 a tonne C&F for March/April shipment based on Chinese origin, or at $140.60 from the U.S. Gulf, or $141.40 from the U.S. Pacific northwest.
But earlier Philippines Agriculture Secretary Salvador Escudero contradicted local traders and told Reuters in Manila that the deal had not yet been concluded.
"We are still negotiating on a government-to-government basis. The volume will depend on the price China is willing to sell to us," he said.
"Our corn importation this year will depend on the needs of the poultry and livestock sectors," Escudero added.
